Search a whole folder without leaving the editor. More at [www.malgel.com](https://www.malgel.com).

## New

- **Find in Files** (Ctrl+Shift+F). Type what you are looking for and Malgel searches the text of every file under the open folder, listing the lines that hold it as `path:line` and the line itself. Confirming a line opens that file with the caret on it.
  - The same walk Quick Open uses, so `.gitignore` is respected.
  - Files that are not text are skipped rather than guessed at.
  - Smart case, as in VS Code: `smoke` finds `SMOKE` too, while `SMOKE` finds only the shouty one.

This is the last piece of the VS Code alignment: earlier releases gained the command palette, file-type icons, the aligned key bindings, the Explorer's own keys (new file and folder, rename with F2, delete, cut, copy and paste) and Find in Files' neighbour, Quick Open.

## Downloads

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) | `Malgel-0.1.2-macos-arm64.dmg`: open it and drag Malgel to Applications |
| Windows 10+ | `Malgel-0.1.2-windows-x64-setup.exe` (installer) or `Malgel-0.1.2-windows-x64.zip` (portable) |
| Linux x86_64 | `Malgel-0.1.2-x86_64.AppImage` (`chmod +x` it, then run it) or `malgel-0.1.2-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

The macOS app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so Gatekeeper blocks it after download: right-click it and choose Open once, or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Malgel.app`. The Windows files are unsigned: SmartScreen may warn, and **More info → Run anyway** gets past it. `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists every file's checksum.
